title: Churn precursor inventory and logbook
content:
Churn Precursor Inventory & Logbook — working doc

Purpose:
- Capture a canonical list of signals we believe precede churn or renewal friction.
- Propose a pragmatic scoring prototype (0-100) and mapping to automated risk flags + playbooks.
- Log examples, edge cases, and measurement sources for calibration.

Background / context:
- Multiple CS stakeholders asked for a single source of truth we can iterate on. Existing scorecards are fractured across sheets. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: signals we can compute today (or within 2 sprints).
- Goal: get a 1st-pass composite health metric we can show in QBRs and in the renewal tracker; iterate weighting based on outcomes (renewal/lost) over next 6 months.

Inventory (signal categories and example metrics):

1) Consumption & Usage (owner: analytics)
   - MAU / DAU trend (30d slope). (source: product telemetry)
   - Active routes / API calls per seat (rolling 7d).
   - Key feature adoption (e.g., embeddings, fine-tuning calls) — binary flag if <10% of expected cohort.
   - Late warning: sudden drop >40% week-over-week.

2) Adoption & ROI signals (owner: cs)
   - Number of customer-created workflows in prod.
   - Number of user-facing successes (internal metric: 3 wins logged in 90d).
   - Time-to-first-value (TTFV) vs SLA (if > baseline by 2x => risk).

3) Financial & Contract signals (owner: finance)
   - Over/under utilization vs committed (>=120% spike or <=30% usage).
   - Payment anomalies / invoice disputes in last 90d.
   - Upcoming renewal date within 90 days (binary; multiplies risk weight).

4) Support & Reliability (owner: support)
   - P1/P2 incidents in last 90d (count + time to resolution).
   - Escalations to engineering.
   - Negative NPS from recent support interaction (<6).

5) Executive & Stakeholder engagement (owner: cs)
   - Exec sponsor at risk? (last exec touch >180d => negative)
   - Renewal negotiation status (open/closed/paused) — qualitative tag.

6) Security & Compliance (owner: security)
   - Required compliance gaps raised (e.g., SOC/ISO audit issues unresolved).
   - Private deployment/networking blockers outstanding.

Signal normalization & example weighting (PROTOTYPE):
- Normalize each signal to 0-100 (0 worst, 100 best). For binary flags, map true=>0/100 depending on polarity.
- Proposed category weights (sum=100):
   Consumption: 30
   Adoption/ROI: 25
   Financial: 15
   Support/Reliability: 15
   Exec Engagement: 10
   Security/Compliance: 5

Composite score = sum(category_score * category_weight)/100.
Risk tiers (initial thresholds):
   - High risk: composite <= 40  => trigger immediate SLA playbook + AE/CSM alert
   - Medium risk: 41-65 => targeted outreach + product onboarding runbook
   - Healthy: >65 => standard enablement cadence

Playbook mapping (quick sketches):
- High risk (<=40):
   1) Auto-create "renewal watch" in CRM + notify CSM + AE.
   2) 48-hour triage call with customer + incident review (if recent reliability issues).
   3) Offer temporary usage credits / technical deep-dive.
   4) Escalate to Solutions Eng if product-fit issue suspected.
- Medium risk (41-65):
   1) Personalized enablement plan (1-3 sessions).
   2) Share ROI case studies + quick wins checklist.
   3) Schedule exec check-in if date within 90d.
- Healthy (>65):
   1) Continue standard QBR cadence.
   2) Highlight expansion opportunities.

Example logbook entries (realistic, anonymized):
- Customer: OrionHealth (example)
   Signals: DAU drop 55% WoW; 2 P2 incidents; billing dispute open; exec last met 240d ago.
   Normalized category scores: Consumption 20, Support 40, Financial 30, Adoption 50, Exec 10, Security 90 -> composite ~ 31 => HIGH RISK
   Action: CSM flagged, 48h triage, AE engaged. (note: product team investigating P2 root cause)

- Customer: LuminaFinance
   Signals: steady usage + spike in embeddings; renewal in 120d; no incidents; payment on time.
   Composite ~ 78 => HEALTHY

- Customer: AtlasRetail
   Signals: low feature adoption, underutilized commit (35%); exec contact monthly.
   Composite ~ 58 => MEDIUM RISK
   Action: schedule adoption sprint + billing review.

Data sources & ownership: 
- Telemetry: infra/analytics pipeline (events.emp -> bigquery or telemetry table). Owner: Analytics Team (Jacob Lin).
- Billing / Usage: Finance (Priya Nair).
- Support tickets / Escalations: Support repo + Zendesk (Evan Brooks).
- CSM notes: CRM (HubSpot) and internal CS notes (owner: CSM assigned).

Measurement notes & pitfalls:
- Private deployments: telemetry gaps for on-prem customers; fallback to proxy metrics (billing, support).
- Short-lived spikes: weekly smoothing recommended (7-14d) to avoid false positives.
- Weight bias: early experiments may overfit to Support signals; need holdout evaluation (cohort of closed renewals vs churn over 6 months).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should renewal proximity be a multiplicative factor rather than additive? (TODO: test both)
- Q: Which historical horizon yields best predictive power? 30d vs 90d? (run A/B retrospective)
- Build: analytics needs a scheduled pipeline for composite score + dashboard (JIRA-CS-1489).
- Owner assignments: confirm coverage for security signals for on-prem customers. (action: @Priya)

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
1) This week: finalize canonical list of signals and owners (ask owners to sign off).
2) 2-week sprint: analytics to produce daily composite score pipeline + export to CRM.
3) 1 month: run backtest on past 12 months (AGG: renewals vs lost) and update weights.
4) 2 months: add playbook automation (alerts, runbook attachments, Slack workflows).

Notes to self / quick scribbles:
- Keep playbooks tightly scoped, avoid "do all checks" — we need priority.
- Avoid scoring churn purely on usage; financial + exec engagement are high-value signals for enterprise.
- Consider cohort-specific weights (startups vs enterprise).

References / links:
- Confluence plan: https://redwood-confluence.internal/CS/health-scoring-playbook
- Backtest ticket: JIRA-CS-1499
- Slack thread: #cs-ops (renewal-signal-tuning)

Revision log:
- 2024-10-18: initial draft (S. Alvarez)
- 2024-11-04: added private-deployments notes and security signals (Priya)
- 2025-02-14: updated weighting prototype after CS sync (Jacob)

Unresolved: need to decide if we surface raw signals or only composite score in QBRs — raw signals helpful for context but can confuse execs.

END OF DOC
